Getting started with glass.sqdaitools

Source: vignettes/glass-quickstart.Rmd
glass-quickstart.Rmd
library(glass.sqdaitools)

This vignette walks through the GLASS data lifecycle covered by the package: registry lookups, tile mapping, DOY folders, downloading and post-processing. Dataset-bound chunks run offline; anything that touches the network is shown with eval = FALSE so the vignette builds without connectivity.

The product registry

The registry has one row per archive variant (product x source x resolution) observed under https://glass.hku.hk/archive/:

glass_registry(verified_only = TRUE)[, c("variant_id", "res", "cadence_days",
                                         "observed_years", "url_root")]

Variants with verified = TRUE were checked against real granules: file naming fragments (code, version, layer), year coverage, and band metadata (fill_value, scale_factor, valid_min/valid_max) all come from that check and are consumed by glass_read()/glass_process().

From region of interest to tiles

Tiled GLASS products reuse the MODIS sinusoidal h<v> grid. Rebuild the exact tile polygons and see which ones your study area needs:

# 一个 2-3 km 缓冲的点(上海人民广场周边)
roi <- sf::st_buffer(
  sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(c(121.47, 31.23)), crs = 4326),
  3000
)
tiles <- glass_tiles_for_sf(roi)
tiles[, c("h", "v", "lon_min", "lon_max", "lat_min", "lat_max", "valid")]
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 7 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 115.4701 ymin: 30 xmax: 143.5948 ymax: 40
#> Geodetic CRS:  WGS 84
#>    h v  lon_min  lon_max lat_min lat_max valid                       geometry
#> 1 28 5 115.4701 143.5948      30      40  TRUE POLYGON ((130.5407 40, 143....

For straight bounding boxes there is glass_tiles_for_bbox(), and passing the resulting table directly to glass_fetch() is allowed (it understands data frames with h/v columns).

Date range to composite folders

The archive stores one folder per composite start day-of-year:

glass_doys("LAI_MODIS_250M", from = "2018-08-01", to = "2018-08-31")
#> # A tibble: 5 × 4
#>    year   doy date       folder
#>   <int> <int> <date>     <chr> 
#> 1  2018   209 2018-07-28 209   
#> 2  2018   217 2018-08-05 217   
#> 3  2018   225 2018-08-13 225   
#> 4  2018   233 2018-08-21 233   
#> 5  2018   241 2018-08-29 241

mode = "span" (default) keeps composites partially overlapping the range; mode = "start" keeps only those starting inside it.

Finding and downloading files

glass_list_files() reads one composite folder’s listing; glass_fetch() loops it over the DOY table and downloads with resume/verification:

files <- glass_fetch(
  "LAI_MODIS_250M",
  from = "2018-08-01", to = "2018-12-31",
  roi = roi,
  out_dir = "data/glass/lai"
)
# 用 dry_run = TRUE 先看清单,不下载

The download engine compares sizes with the server, resumes .part files via HTTP Range, and writes glass_manifest.csv into out_dir, so an interrupted run continues where it stopped.

Post-processing

glass_process() is the parameterised pipeline: cleanup, mosaic, reproject, mask, optional temporal collapse:

mean_lai <- glass_process(
  files,
  roi = roi,
  product = "LAI_MODIS_250M",
  method = "cubic",
  fun = "mean",
  outfile = "glass_lai_mean.tif"
)

Band cleanup comes from the registry: the raw fill (e.g. 255) maps to NA after scaling, and the valid scaled range is excluded from analysis. For an already-read SpatRaster, glass_read() with no product is a no-op except for explicit fill/valid_range arguments.

Interactive UI 

glass_app()

Draw the ROI on a map, pick a verified variant, preview the manifest and download — the same package functions underneath. The output folder can be chosen through the built-in, in-page directory browser (or typed directly) and a progress bar follows each file during the batch download.
